# Vendor/

Self-contained MuPDF build from upstream source, keeping `swift build` independent
of Homebrew or other system installs.

## Contents

- `build-mupdf.sh` — downloads the official MuPDF source tarball
  (`https://mupdf.com/downloads/archive/mupdf-<version>-source.tar.gz`), verifies its
  pinned SHA-256 checksum, and compiles `MuPDF.xcframework`.
- `MUPDF_VERSION` — the upstream tag currently targeted (1.28.6).
- `patches/` — upstream commits cherry-picked onto that tag, applied in order by
  `build-mupdf.sh`. **The build is 1.28.6 plus these backports, not stock 1.28.6**;
  see [Backported patches](#backported-patches).
- `MuPDF.xcframework` — generated by `build-mupdf.sh` and excluded from Git. A single
  combined static library (MuPDF core + bundled thirdparty codecs), arm64 (Apple Silicon)
  only, built with PDF JavaScript (mujs) and OCR (tesseract/leptonica) disabled.
  Consumed by `Package.swift` as a local `.binaryTarget`.

The corresponding public C headers are vendored separately at
`Sources/MuPDFBridge/include/mupdf/` (needed for `#include <mupdf/fitz.h>`
in `MuPDFBridge.h`) — `build-mupdf.sh` updates both together.

## Backported patches

`MuPDF.xcframework` is MuPDF 1.28.6 with these upstream fixes cherry-picked, applied in order
(`git format-patch` output of each commit, unchanged unless noted), because no release has
them yet. They were taken from master between 19 October and 2 November 2026; none is on the
1.28.x branch or in any release as of 2026-11-04.

| Patch | Upstream commit (master) | Bug | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0001` | [`5ba5c976`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/5ba5c976427aa2c084d21e43e71f5f8d4eb87105) | Bug 709849 | A store lookup read the cache entry after unlocking, so another thread could free it first. Crashed VectorPDF in `pdf_load_font` and `fz_icc_transform_color` when documents were used on several threads at once. |
| `0002` | [`299d8464`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/299d8464f1a86df6d056e11d8850135fcac7eec7) | Bug 709849 | A new store entry could be found, used and freed by another thread before it was linked in. |
| `0003` | [`4ed1a6dc`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/4ed1a6dc3b65f25f88818f76f63f940dd7fed620) | Bug 709849 | Store keys could match PDF objects from different documents, which upsets store entries when several documents are open. |
| `0004` | [`4d84a591`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/4d84a591e69a0a567a497b6c3ba25d38d722acda) | Bug 709836 | Out-of-bounds read in linearization hints. **Rebased:** two context lines differ in 1.28.6 (a debug message's `%d`); the fix is unchanged. |
| `0005` | [`ce44d4cc`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/ce44d4cc6b93f9af6dde3a07245305be6e0207d2) | Bug 709840 | PDF objects leaked when writing a PDF (Save). |
| `0006` | [`e24a84b6`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/e24a84b67d864b0e685bc18ea72ac3ecbe62cfe9) | Bug 709892 | The content filter dropped text drawn outside `BT`/`ET`. `pdf_redact_page` (Redaction) rewrites pages through it. |
| `0007` | [`97a78ae3`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/97a78ae35a9d1a41bf4563c3049c5af0ebd8c6b1) | Bug 709894 | The content filter mishandled fonts set up in an ExtGState. |
| `0008` | [`1ed719e7`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/1ed719e70e4273e475473cd16afd2256bcafb6ba) | Bug 709885 | Reverts a change to stream EOF handling that broke some files. |
| `0009` | [`37d283e0`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/37d283e0752862999f6ff7947e69d86a4d1f698b) | Bug 709904 | The content filter scaled text wrongly. A redaction on the PDF Association's `NegativeFontSize.pdf` deleted about 180 characters outside the redacted area. |
| `0010` | [`084ded78`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/084ded78a905e13f19fe3ed473a54f822115237b) | Bug 709907 | The content filter mishandled pattern colours. |
| `0011` | [`e1d5bfc0`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/e1d5bfc0cd9e8f7f52d7a7fdb128335c358ec580) | Bug 709913 | The content filter mishandled Type 3 fonts. |
| `0012` | [`a9e17fa8`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/a9e17fa86c40eac0b1eec2e4445ffd4db9abb022) | Bug 709906 | The content filter mishandled inline images with inline colorspaces. |
| `0013` | [`15c14388`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/15c1438895e4c7a3605b677fe1435817572cec0f) | Bug 709903 | Undefined characters in structured text (selection, search, copying). |
| `0014` | [`644dada0`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/644dada08fd527e9c54f765ea2432efbe6c8b3a7) | Bug 709888 | Glyph clipping when rendering. |
| `0015` | [`e38993af`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/e38993af8b9be637d9662f9f291165ad06f15505) | Bug 709905 | The content filter didn't flush the stroke state when filtering stroked text. |
| `0016` | [`377f3f13`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/377f3f13b436b7d19c6a93e0caa06b5afe3ad7d3) | Bug 709940 | Very deeply nested objects in a corrupt or malicious PDF could exhaust the stack. |
| `0017` | [`6217a2e8`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/6217a2e8bc340072e60cfca421e64d279bf48dca) | Bug 709915 | Paths' bounds in display lists were too small, so parts of drawings could be cut off; the render actor caches pages as display lists. |
| `0018` | [`edd7a81c`](https://github.com/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commit/edd7a81ca0f724ccffc425209f9cfa4fde5fe706) | Bug 709910 | Invalid `Resources` entries were silently ignored rather than handled. |

Not taken, as of 2026-11-04:
- `4ed88915` (Bug 709881, empty clip paths), `3b4fc7cd` (Bug 709937) and `ede72b82` (Bug 709936),
  more content-filter fixes: they build on master's other filter changes (such as `54559c9d`),
  which don't apply to 1.28.6 on their own. Take them with the release that has them.
- `e44f8ed6` (Bug 709868): fixes `fz_parse_data_uri_with_media_type`, which 1.28.6 doesn't have.
- The 1.28.x branch's 53 fixes since 1.28.6 (crashes, double frees, overflows): wait for 1.28.7.

**Rebase onto the first release that includes them**: move to that tag (below) and delete
the patches it contains, so the build is a stock release again. `build-mupdf.sh` stops
with an error if a patch no longer applies, which is the cue to check whether it's
upstream. `ConcurrencyStressTests` (`VECTORPDF_STRESS_TESTS=1 swift test --filter
ConcurrencyStress`) reproduced the crash every run without these fixes; run it after any
MuPDF change.

To add another backport: `gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.patch"
repos/ArtifexSoftware/mupdf/commits/<sha> > Vendor/patches/000N-<subject>.patch`,
add a row above, and rebuild.

## Bumping the MuPDF version

1. Pick the new release tag from https://mupdf.com/releases/history, and check which
   of the [backported patches](#backported-patches) it includes.
2. `./Vendor/build-mupdf.sh <new-version>` — it downloads the tarball, verifies
   it against the pinned sha256 in the script (update `MUPDF_SHA256` there
   first, or export `MUPDF_SHA256=...` for a one-off run, using the value the
   script prints on a mismatch after you've verified the download), builds,
   and overwrites `Vendor/MuPDF.xcframework` and
   `Sources/MuPDFBridge/include/mupdf/`.
3. Update `Vendor/MUPDF_VERSION` and the default in `build-mupdf.sh`. Delete the
   patches the release includes (the build fails on them) and their table rows.
4. `swift build && swift test`, skim upstream `CHANGES` for anything that
   touches APIs this app calls (`Sources/MuPDFBridge/MuPDFBridge.c`), then
   commit.

The script's own output flags two known Clang-Modules pitfalls from vendoring
someone else's header tree wholesale under an `umbrella header` (which sweeps
in every physical file under the directory, whether or not it's actually
`#include`d):
- A new header-guardless X-macro-style snippet header (like
  `mupdf/pdf/name-table.h`) needs a `textual header "mupdf/..."` entry in
  `include/module.modulemap`, or Clang corrupts its mid-declaration textual
  inclusion with cryptic "expected identifier" parse errors.
- A new header unreachable from `fitz.h`/`pdf.h` (like `mupdf/html.h`) needs
  an `exclude header "mupdf/..."` entry, or every build prints a "does not
  include header" warning for it.
Both are just noise/warnings the script surfaces proactively so a version
bump doesn't have to rediscover them the hard way; add the printed line(s) to
`include/module.modulemap` and re-run.

## Why not link against Homebrew's mupdf?

Homebrew's formula builds against system freetype/harfbuzz/openjpeg/etc and
enables JS + OCR by default, which means: (a) an extra install step for every
contributor/CI machine, (b) hardcoded `/opt/homebrew` paths that break on
Intel Macs or non-Homebrew setups, and (c) a build that can silently change
underneath the app on `brew upgrade`. Building from MuPDF's own source
tarball with its bundled thirdparty libraries avoids all three and pins an
exact, reproducible version.

## Why not a prebuilt MuPDF XCFramework from someone else?

There isn't one to reuse — checked as of this writing there's no official or
actively-maintained community MuPDF XCFramework/Swift package (Swift Package
Index and GitHub searches both come up empty). If that changes upstream, it
would be worth revisiting.
